name: NRTK Ratel-S

placement_rationale.text: Ratel-S's three roles — transport, remote mine-laying, and kamikaze use — are all close-in tasks that have to happen at or just behind the line itself, squarely inside doctrine.md's 1-5km close-reconnaissance band rather than a rear logistics depth. Its EW-hardening is itself evidence of a close siting: that hardening only matters where jamming density is highest, which is near the contact line, not in the rear.

characteristics: Multifunctional: transportation, remote mine-laying, and kamikaze (self-detonating) use
Strength: Stable operation under electronic warfare conditions; flexible role (can be reconfigured for different missions)
Limitation: Small compact platform, limited payload relative to larger logistics UGVs
Estimated quantity available: Fielded numbers not publicly disclosed
employment_notes: Represents the ground equivalent of the FPV drone's 'miner'/kamikaze pattern described in the FPV tactics reference, extended to a wheeled ground platform
contrast_vs_traditional: A ground robot that can mine, deliver a kamikaze charge, or simply transport supplies depending on how it's fitted reflects the same doctrine.md force-structure pattern documented for drone units: small, cheap, remotely operated platforms procured and adapted at unit level for whatever the sector needs, rather than issued as a single-purpose system from a central program.
